items.text: Extra small text (xs) — fine print, footnotes, legal copy
Small text (sm) — secondary information, captions, metadata
Base text (base) — default body copy, paragraphs, descriptions
Large text (lg) — lead paragraphs, introductions, callouts
Extra large text (xl) — hero descriptions, feature highlights, key messages
Light weight — airy, delicate text for subtle content
Normal weight — standard body text weight
Medium weight — slightly emphasised text
Semibold weight — moderate emphasis for subheadings
Bold weight — strong emphasis for important content
Extrabold weight — maximum emphasis for critical text
Text colour — default body text
Muted colour — secondary, less prominent text
Accent colour — highlighted, drawn-attention text
Link colour — interactive, clickable appearance
Inherit colour — takes parent's colour
Tight leading — compact text, good for headings and badges. This line wraps to show the reduced space between lines of text in a multi-line paragraph.
Snug leading — slightly tighter than normal, good for cards. This line wraps to show the snug space between lines of text in a multi-line paragraph.
Normal leading — standard body text. This line wraps to show the normal space between lines of text in a multi-line paragraph.
Relaxed leading — generous spacing, good for readability. This line wraps to show the relaxed space between lines of text in a multi-line paragraph.
Body font — primary reading font (Quicksand)
Body alt font — alternative body font
Handwriting font — informal, personal feel
Mono font — code, technical, tabular data
Left aligned text — the default reading direction for LTR languages. Most body text should be left aligned for optimal readability.
Centre aligned text — used for headings, quotes, and short decorative text. Not recommended for long paragraphs.
Right aligned text — used sparingly for specific design elements, dates, or numerical columns.
Paragraph element (p) — default block text
Span element — inline text
Div element — generic container text
Small element — fine print, legal
Strong element — important text
Em element — emphasised text
Blockquote element — quoted content with attribution
This text is clamped to 1 line. It should truncate with an ellipsis if it exceeds the available width of the container. Extra content here to test the truncation behaviour at different widths.

This text is clamped to 2 lines. It should show up to two lines of content and truncate with an ellipsis after that point. Extra content here to demonstrate multi-line clamping works correctly across different screen sizes.

This text is clamped to 3 lines. It should display three full lines of content before adding an ellipsis for overflow. This is useful for card descriptions, excerpts, and preview text where space is limited but you want to show more than a single line summary.
Light tone — for use on dark backgrounds
Dark tone — for use on light backgrounds
UPPERCASE TEXT
Flush text (no margin)
AAC enabled text — shows pictogram cards when content-aac is on
Large bold accent text for hero descriptions
SMALL UPPERCASE MUTED TEXT FOR LABELS
Medium semibold relaxed for comfortable reading at length. This combination is ideal for long-form content where readability is the priority.
Extra large light handwriting for a personal touch
Clamped accent bold — 2 lines max. This card preview shows accent colour with bold weight, clamped to two lines with ellipsis overflow for consistent card heights.

The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. This sentence contains every letter of the English alphabet and is commonly used to test typography. It demonstrates how the font handles different letter combinations, spacing, and kerning across a natural reading flow. When reviewing typography, pay attention to how letters like 'fi', 'fl', and 'ff' interact, and whether the overall rhythm of the text feels balanced and comfortable for extended reading.
